thread:
jamie: Kicking off a small canary for neptune-7b-ephemeral in catalog at 22:00 UTC. Target: 2% traffic, 1h observation. Need fallback ordering check and rollback ledger set.
sara: ACK. I'll own telemetry gating (latency, 5xx, quality signals). Will set alerts and a quick eval runbook.
alex: FYI, model has a variant 'neptune-7b-ephemeral-quant' that'll be second in fallback. We should make fallback order explicit: primary -> quant -> last-resort-13b.
morgan: +1 on explicit ordering. Also suggest enabling KV-cache warmup for the canary nodes to avoid cold-tail latencies.
jamie: good. Can we pin traffic at routing level so canary doesn't get evicted by autoscaler during the window? Need deploybot guard.
luis: I'll add a pin tag to the catalog entry: pin:canary/7932101111. That prevents evict until we lift pin.
deploy-bot: deploybot: starting canary rollout for catalog entry neptune-7b-ephemeral (id: ce-3345) -> 2% traffic on eu/na. Change window 22:00-23:00 UTC. CI checks green.
sara: Telemetry rules I'm adding: latency p95 increase > 120ms OR 5xx rate > 0.5% OR quality regression > 1.5% -> automatic rollback. I'll push alerts to #eng-oncall and email owners.
ops-bot: ops-bot: canary monitoring stream started. Grouping by region and model_variant. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/rollouts/neptune-7932101111
alex: One more: fallback ordering needs TTL semantics. If quant variant is chosen but hits memory pressure, it should fall back to last-resort-13b, not requeue to primary. Set TTL 30s.
morgan: Added config snippet to catalog flag 'fallback_ttl_seconds: 30' and 'fallback_mode: immediate'.
jamie: deploy-bot, please record a rollback ledger entry if we trigger the gate. We want a single-line summary with reason and who ack'd the rollback.
deploy-bot: deploybot: acknowledged. Ledger entry template: `ledger_id: <ts>-ce3345 | action: rollback | reason: <alert> | by: <person>`; will auto-post to thread on action.
sara: During the first 25m we saw an intermittent p95 spike in eu (up 40ms) but 5xx stayed low. I held at 2% and started a targeted eval set — no quality drop. Looks safe so far.
luis: Autoscaler observed slight memory churn on quant nodes. Not yet critical. I've bumped quant pool headroom by 10% for the window.
ops-bot: ops-bot: abort threshold breached in na at 00:12: p95 +210ms, 5xx 0.7% -> triggering staged rollback.
jamie: Rolling back now. deploy-bot, run ledger entry and lift pins.
deploy-bot: deploybot: executing rollback for ce-3345. ledger_id: 7932101167-ce3345 | action: rollback | reason: na_latency_spike+5xx | by: jamie
luis: Pin removed. Traffic shifted back to primary variants. Confirming drain of canary connections.
sara: Telemetry confirms latency back to baseline. Creating a short post-rollback checklist: dump heap profiles for quant pool, capture sample traces for 00:00-00:15, re-run quality eval.
alex: We'll reschedule a narrower window tomorrow with smaller burst and KV warmup earlier. Also add a canary abort escalation to oncall runbook.
morgan: Noted for release notes: "neptune-7b-ephemeral canary started and rolled back due to NA latency spike; no quality regression observed; follow-up investigation scheduled." Will draft.
jamie: thanks all. Good runbook iteration. Closing thread once Morgan posts release note blurb and Ops attaches heap traces.
